summary: The narrator, after a biker ambush in the desert, accepts a ride from the PI Tresting, who offers to share intel. Their exchange covers Tresting's jammed Glock, his backup Beretta, and the narrator's earlier gift of a snub-nosed revolver to a girl named Penny. The two search the dead bikers, finding high-tech night vision gear and plastic explosives but no clue to why the gang wanted the narrator dead. The narrator takes grenades from a Harley saddlebag and climbs into Tresting's beat-up truck.
one_line: After a desert biker ambush, the narrator accepts a ride from PI Tresting, searches the gang's gear, and loads grenades into his truck.
key_facts: Tresting offers the narrator a lift into town and to share intel after the biker ambush.
The narrator slides a SIG back into their coat and considers that they could still kill Tresting if necessary.
Tresting says he will pretend he didn't see the extended magazine on the narrator's gun.
The narrator says the extended magazine is legal two hundred miles east of there.
The narrator's bike went down in the desert scrub, and Tresting reports it is a lost cause.
Tresting's Glock is banged up and jammed; he clears the chamber and tucks it into his belt without reloading.
Tresting carries a Beretta as a backup, which is nine-millimeter.
The narrator says the snub-nosed revolver was given to a little girl as a party favor, referring to Penny.
The narrator searches the bikers and finds high-tech night vision gear and plastic explosives.
The search turns up no clue indicating what brought the gang there, except that they wanted the narrator dead.
The narrator loads grenades and other weapons from a Harley saddlebag into a bag.
Tresting's truck is a beat-up old clunker, and the narrator stows the bag of weapons on its floor.
